name: ZITLAS Jowar Roti with Peanut Curry
description: A sorghum (jowar) flatbread served with a light peanut-based curry — a new grain base paired with a curry rather than a dry chutney.
instructions: Knead jowar flour with warm water (it needs warm water to bind) and pat into a flatbread; cook on a hot tawa.
For the curry, heat oil, temper cumin, add tomato and cook soft, then stir in ground peanuts with water to form a light curry.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Serve the roti hot with the peanut curry.
why_it_works: Jowar is a distinct gluten-free grain from bajra or ragi already in the database
Curry format (not dry chutney) changes how the peanuts are eaten
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Foxtail Millet Pongal
description: A South Indian pongal made with foxtail millet and moong dal, tempered with ghee, pepper and cumin — a distinct one-pot format from any upma or khichdi.
ingredients: Black pepper, cumin seeds, ginger — 4 g
instructions: Dry-roast moong dal lightly, then pressure cook with foxtail millet and water (1:4 ratio) for 3 whistles until soft and porridge-like.
Heat ghee, temper crushed black pepper, cumin seeds and chopped ginger.
Pour the tempering over the cooked pongal and mix.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Pongal's soft, tempered rice-porridge technique is genuinely different from khichdi or upma preparation
Foxtail millet swap keeps the traditional method but changes the grain profile
Traditional South Indian temple food reframed as a fitness breakfast

name: ZITLAS Lobia Salad Bowl
description: A no-cook salad of boiled black-eyed peas (lobia) with onion, tomato and lemon — introducing a legume not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Toss boiled lobia with onion and tomato.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately.
why_it_works: Lobia is a genuinely new legume for the database, broadening protein-source diversity as required
Entirely no-cook
High fiber, low cost

name: ZITLAS Whole Green Gram Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with whole cooked green gram (moong, not split) — a chunkier, whole-legume filling distinct from the split-dal Moong Dal Paratha.
ingredients: Whole green gram, boiled and mashed — 90 g
Cumin powder, ginger, green chilli — 5 g
instructions: Boil whole green gram until soft, drain well and mash coarsely with cumin powder, ginger and green chilli.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the filling and seal.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Whole-bean texture is noticeably different from the smoother split-dal paratha already in the database
Uses the whole legume including its skin, adding extra fiber
Different pulse-paratha option from sattu, rajma or soya

name: ZITLAS Curd Rice with Pomegranate
description: Classic curd rice finished with fresh pomegranate seeds instead of the usual peanut tempering — a distinct sweet-tart variation.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, oil — 4 ml
instructions: Mash the cold rice slightly and mix with curd.
Quickly temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a few drops of oil and stir in.
Top generously with fresh pomegranate seeds just before serving.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Pomegranate adds a fresh, antioxidant-rich topping genuinely different from the peanut version already in the database
Almost entirely no-cook
Visually distinct and appealing for repeat use

name: ZITLAS Ragi Idli
description: Steamed idli made from a ragi-flour-enriched batter — a fourth distinct grain base for idli in the database, after rava, soya granule and paneer-stuffed.
instructions: Mix ragi flour into the fermented idli batter, adding a little water to keep it pourable.
Rest 10 minutes.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes in a pressure cooker without the whistle.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: Ragi adds calcium and fiber not present in a plain rice-urad idli
Distinct from the other three idli variants already in the database by using ragi specifically
Still fully steamed, no added fat

name: ZITLAS Horse Gram (Kulith) Usal Bowl
description: A Maharashtrian-style usal made from sprouted horse gram (kulith) — an iron-rich legume distinct from moong, chana or matki already used in the database's usal recipes.
ingredients: Horse gram, sprouted and boiled — 120 g
Goda masala or garam masala — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook soft.
Add boiled horse gram and goda masala with a little water; simmer 6-8 minutes.
Serve hot as a bowl, with lemon if liked.
why_it_works: Horse gram is notably higher in iron than the other legumes already used for usal in the database
Traditionally considered warming and used in winter cooking
One-pan, genuinely regional

name: ZITLAS Peanut Chutney Idli Bowl
description: Plain steamed idli broken into a bowl and tossed with peanut chutney and a warm tempering — a deconstructed idli format distinct from serving idli whole with a side.
instructions: Steam idlis as usual and let cool slightly.
Grind peanuts with garlic, red chilli and a little water into a thick chutney.
Break the idlis into bite-sized pieces into a bowl.
Toss with the peanut chutney and a mustard-seed tempering in hot oil.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Broken-and-tossed format is a genuinely different eating experience from whole idli with a side dip
Peanut chutney coats every piece rather than being used for dipping
Repurposes the same idli technique in a distinct way

name: ZITLAS Masoor Dal Cheela
description: A savoury crepe made from ground red lentil (masoor dal) batter — a different pulse base from moong, chana or besan cheelas.
ingredients: Masoor dal, soaked and ground — 60 g
instructions: Grind soaked masoor dal with a little water into a smooth batter.
Mix in onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Masoor dal is a distinct pulse from moong, chana or besan already used for cheelas in the database
Cooks quickly since masoor dal doesn't need long soaking
Mild flavour, easy to season either way

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Urad Dal Vada Bowl
description: Urad dal vadas air-fried and served dry with chutney rather than soaked in curd — a distinct bowl format from the Air-Fried Moong Dahi Vada.
ingredients: Urad dal, soaked and ground — 100 g
instructions: Grind soaked urad dal with ginger and green chilli into a thick, fluffy batter (whip well for airiness).
Shape into small discs with a hole in the centre and brush with oil.
Air fry at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden.
Serve dry with coconut chutney on the side, not soaked in curd.
why_it_works: Dry-with-chutney serving is a genuinely different eating experience from the curd-soaked moong version already in the database
Air frying keeps this far lower in fat than a traditional deep-fried vada
Classic South Indian breakfast made lighter

name: ZITLAS Little Millet Upma
description: Upma made with little millet (kutki) instead of rava — a different, less common millet from the foxtail or bajra versions already in the database.
instructions: Rinse the little millet and soak for 15 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute vegetables 3 minutes.
Add the soaked millet and water in a 1:2.5 ratio, cover and simmer 12-15 minutes until soft.
Fluff and serve hot.
why_it_works: Little millet is a genuinely uncommon grain outside dedicated millet cooking, broadening grain diversity as required
Lower glycemic impact than rava
Same familiar upma technique, different base grain

name: ZITLAS Brown Chana Chaat Wrap
description: A tangy brown chana chaat wrapped inside a roti — combining a no-cook chaat filling with a cooked wrap base, distinct from the chana chaat toast.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti; keep warm.
Toss boiled brown chana with onion, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Spoon the chana chaat onto the warm roti and roll tightly.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Wrap format is a genuinely different way to eat chana chaat from piling it on toast
Portable for a commute unlike the open toast version
Brown chana has a nuttier flavour than white chana

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Moth Bean Cutlet
description: Sprouted matki (moth bean) mashed and shaped into pan-fried cutlets — a distinct patty format from the wet Matki Usal Bowl already in the database.
ingredients: Sprouted matki, boiled and mashed — 100 g
instructions: Mash boiled matki with onion, rice flour and spices until it holds together.
Shape into small flat cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Patty format, unlike the wet usal bowl already using the same legume, gives a genuinely different eating experience
Crisp exterior contrasts with the soft usal version
Good lunchbox-style option

name: ZITLAS Jowar Bhakri with Curd and Peanuts
description: A thick, hand-patted jowar bhakri (not rolled like a roti) served with curd and roasted peanuts — a distinct bread-making technique from the thinner Jowar Roti earlier in this batch.
instructions: Knead jowar flour with warm water and pat out by hand into a thick round (bhakri is patted, not rolled with a pin).
Cook on a hot tawa until browned on both sides, brushing with a little ghee.
Serve with a side of curd and roasted peanuts.
why_it_works: Hand-patted bhakri technique produces a thicker, denser bread than a rolled roti, genuinely different eating experience
Traditional Maharashtrian rural breakfast combination
Curd and peanuts on the side supply protein the grain lacks

name: ZITLAS Mixed Vegetable Cutlet Sandwich
description: A pan-fried mixed vegetable cutlet (potato, peas, carrot) sandwiched in toasted bread — a paneer-free, protein-light option balanced by the bread's own protein.
instructions: Mash boiled potato with peas, coriander and green chilli into a firm mixture.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Deliberately paneer-free option per the diversity requirement to not over-rely on paneer for vegetarian recipes
Classic Indian cutlet-sandwich comfort food
Works well as an occasional lower-protein, higher-carb breakfast for variety

name: ZITLAS Palak Besan Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter with a large proportion of blended spinach (palak) mixed in — distinct from a plain besan chilla by making spinach the dominant flavour, not a small addition.
instructions: Blend spinach with a little water into a smooth puree.
Whisk besan with the spinach puree, cumin seeds and ajwain into a batter.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with curd.
why_it_works: Spinach is blended in as the primary liquid, not a minor mix-in, making this genuinely different from a plain chilla with a few chopped greens
Distinct green colour and iron content
Naturally vegan

name: ZITLAS Chana Dal Vegetable Pulao
description: A rice pulao cooked with chana dal (not whole chana) and vegetables — a dal-in-pulao format distinct from the Chana Pulao Bowl, which used boiled whole chana.
instructions: Soak chana dal for 20 minutes.
Heat oil, temper whole spices, saute vegetables 3 minutes, then add rice, soaked chana dal and garam masala.
Add water in the standard ratio and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Fluff and serve hot.
why_it_works: Chana dal (split, quicker-cooking) gives a different texture and cooking time from whole chana used in the earlier Chana Pulao Bowl
One-pot, vegetable-forward preparation
Good family-portion breakfast

name: ZITLAS Peanut Sprouts Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with crushed peanuts and moong sprouts together — a crunchy, textured filling distinct from any smooth dal or paneer stuffing.
instructions: Mix chopped moong sprouts with crushed peanuts, green chilli and coriander for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Crunchy sprout-and-peanut texture is genuinely different from every smooth-filling paratha in the database
Two protein sources combined directly in the stuffing
Distinct bite from any dal-based filling

name: ZITLAS Boiled Egg Chaat Bowl
description: Boiled egg tossed chaat-style with onion, tomato and tangy chutney — distinct from the sprouts-and-lemon Boiled Egg Sprouts Bowl by using a chaat masala and chutney profile instead.
instructions: Chop the boiled eggs into quarters.
Toss with onion, tomato, a spoon of green chutney and chaat masala.
Mix gently and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Chutney-and-chaat-masala flavour profile is distinctly different from the lemon-and-pepper Boiled Egg Sprouts Bowl already in the database
No sprouts, so a genuinely different texture and ingredient set
Entirely no-cook

name: ZITLAS Little Millet Idli
description: Steamed idli made with little millet blended into the batter — a fifth distinct grain base for idli in the database.
ingredients: Little millet, soaked and ground — 100 g
instructions: Soak little millet for 4-6 hours, then grind into a smooth batter and mix with the fermented urad dal batter and curd.
Rest 15 minutes.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Little millet is a genuinely uncommon idli base, giving different fiber and mineral content from rice-based idli
Fifth distinct idli variant in the database, each using a different primary grain or protein strategy
Fully steamed

name: ZITLAS Kodo Millet Khichdi
description: A khichdi made with kodo millet instead of rice — a genuinely different grain base from the bajra khichdi or masala oats khichdi already in the database.
instructions: Rinse kodo millet and moong dal together.
Heat oil, temper cumin seeds, saute vegetables 2-3 minutes, then add the millet-dal mix and turmeric.
Add water (roughly 1:3) and pressure cook for 3 whistles until soft.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Kodo millet is a genuinely uncommon grain outside dedicated millet households, distinct in fiber profile from bajra or oats
Same reliable khichdi technique, different grain base each time keeps the database from feeling repetitive
One-pot, low active effort

name: ZITLAS Peanut Sprouts Dosa
description: A dosa batter enriched with ground peanuts and moong sprouts mixed in — raising both protein and texture, distinct from a plain or ragi dosa.
instructions: Mix ground peanuts and chopped moong sprouts into the fermented dosa batter.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Two mix-ins added directly into the batter give a distinctly different texture (slightly gritty, crunchy) from any other dosa in the database
Higher protein than a plain or ragi dosa
Still cooks with the familiar dosa technique

name: ZITLAS Besan Kadhi Bowl
description: A warm, tangy besan-and-curd kadhi eaten as a breakfast bowl — a wet gravy format entirely distinct from any chilla, dhokla or dosa use of besan in the database.
ingredients: Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 4 g
instructions: Whisk besan into curd and water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and turmeric.
Pour in the besan-curd mixture and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often to prevent curdling, for 10-12 minutes until thickened slightly.
Serve warm in a bowl.
why_it_works: Wet, gravy-style kadhi is a genuinely different besan preparation from every chilla or dhokla elsewhere in the database
Curd base makes this notably higher protein than a plain besan dish
Traditionally a lunch dish, reframed here as a light savoury breakfast bowl

name: ZITLAS Multi-Dal Cheela
description: A cheela batter made from three different dals ground together (masoor, moong and urad) — a broader amino-acid-profile cheela distinct from any single-dal version.
instructions: Grind the three soaked dals together with a little water into a smooth batter.
Mix in onion and cumin seeds.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Combining three pulses at once gives a broader amino acid profile than any single-dal cheela already in the database
Genuinely different flavour from blending three dals rather than using one
Same familiar cheela technique

name: ZITLAS Plain Vegetable Uttapam
description: A basic rice-urad uttapam topped only with vegetables, no protein add-in beyond the batter itself — included specifically to diversify the database with a low-effort, fully traditional option.
instructions: Heat a tawa and pour a thick ladle of batter, spreading only slightly.
Scatter onion and tomato over the top and press gently.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until golden, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney or sambar.
why_it_works: A straightforward traditional option without extra grain or protein mix-ins, useful for users who just want the classic version alongside the enriched variants elsewhere in the database
Fermented batter still provides real protein from the urad dal itself
Simple, fast, familiar

name: ZITLAS Green Peas Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with mashed and spiced green peas (matar) — a seasonal vegetable filling distinct from lauki, beetroot or methi.
ingredients: Green peas, boiled and mashed — 70 g
Ginger, green chilli, garam masala — 5 g
instructions: Mash boiled green peas coarsely with ginger, green chilli and garam masala.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the pea mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Matar (green pea) filling is a distinct seasonal vegetable option from the other stuffed parathas in the database
Naturally sweet filling appeals to a different palate than spiced paneer or dal fillings
Traditional winter-season combination

name: ZITLAS Bengali-Style Egg Curry with Bajra Roti
description: A mustard-oil, panch-phoron-spiced Bengali egg curry served with bajra roti — a distinct regional spice profile and grain pairing from the Egg Curry with Multigrain Roti in Batch 2.
instructions: Knead bajra flour into a dough and pat out into a roti; roast on a tawa.
Heat mustard oil, temper panch phoron, saute onion until golden, add potato and turmeric, cook 5 minutes.
Add water for a light gravy and simmer 5 minutes.
Halve the boiled eggs and add, simmering 2-3 minutes.
Serve hot with the bajra roti.
why_it_works: Panch phoron and mustard oil give a genuinely distinct regional flavour from the garam-masala-based multigrain version already in the database
Bajra roti pairing is different from the multigrain roti used before
Potato addition changes the gravy's texture and heartiness

name: ZITLAS Puffed Rice (Murmura) Bhel Bowl
description: A light, no-cook bhel made from puffed rice, vegetables and tamarind chutney — a genuinely different base ingredient (murmura, not poha) from every other bhel or chaat in the database.
instructions: Combine puffed rice, onion, tomato and peanuts in a bowl.
Add tamarind chutney and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Toss well and eat immediately before the puffed rice softens.
why_it_works: Puffed rice is a genuinely new base ingredient for the database, distinct in texture (light, airy) from poha or semiya used elsewhere
Very low calorie, high volume
Zero cooking, classic Mumbai-street-style bhel at home

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Semiya Upma with Peanuts
description: A fully vegetarian vermicelli upma using peanuts as the only protein add-in — distinct from both the soya and egg vermicelli versions already in the database.
instructions: Dry-roast the vermicelli until light golden; set aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, roast peanuts, then saute vegetables 3 minutes.
Add the roasted vermicelli with hot water (roughly equal volume) and cook covered until absorbed.
why_it_works: Peanut-only protein strategy gives users a soya-free, egg-free vermicelli option, completing the set of three distinct protein approaches to the same base dish
Very budget-friendly
Familiar, quick technique

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Peanut Frankie
description: A frankie roll filled with a spiced mixed-vegetable and crushed-peanut filling — a fully vegan frankie option distinct from the soya and paneer versions already in the database.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti on a tawa until slightly charred at the edges.
Heat oil, saute vegetables until soft, then mix in crushed peanuts.
Spread chutneys on the roti, add the vegetable-peanut filling, and roll tightly.
Serve immediately.
why_it_works: Completes a set of three protein strategies (soya, paneer, peanut) for the same frankie format, letting users pick by preference or budget
Fully vegan and generally the cheapest of the three frankie options
Same proven charred-roti technique

name: ZITLAS Amaranth Leaves (Chaulai) Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with chopped amaranth leaves (chaulai saag) — a leafy green distinct from spinach or methi already used in the database's parathas.
instructions: Blanch the amaranth leaves briefly, squeeze out excess water and chop finely.
Mix with garlic and red chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the leaves mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Amaranth leaves are a distinct leafy green from spinach or methi already used in the database, adding calcium and iron
Genuinely different regional green vegetable choice
Traditional North Indian saag-paratha style

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Khakhra Chaat
description: Multigrain khakhra broken into pieces and tossed chaat-style with curd, chutney and vegetables — distinct from simply spreading peanut butter on whole khakhras.
instructions: Break the khakhra into bite-sized pieces into a bowl.
Add curd, onion, tomato, chaat masala and a spoon of green chutney.
Toss gently and eat immediately, while the khakhra still has some crunch.
why_it_works: Deconstructed chaat format is a genuinely different way to eat khakhra from the simple spread-and-stack version already in the database
Curd adds meaningfully more protein than the peanut butter version
No cooking involved

name: ZITLAS Cowpea (Chawli) Sabzi Roti Roll
description: A wet, spiced cowpea (chawli/lobia) sabzi rolled inside a roti — a cooked-curry roll format distinct from the raw Lobia Salad Bowl earlier in this batch.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into rotis; keep warm.
Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add boiled chawli and garam masala with a splash of water, simmer 8-10 minutes into a slightly wet sabzi.
Spoon onto a roti and roll, letting some gravy soak in.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Cooked, gravy-style preparation gives cowpea a genuinely different role from the raw salad version earlier in this batch
Same legume, two legitimately distinct cooking techniques and eating experiences
Homely, filling breakfast

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Sabudana Vada
description: Sabudana shaped into vadas and air-fried instead of the more common khichdi preparation — a distinct format from the Sabudana Peanut Khichdi already in the database.
instructions: Mix soaked sabudana with mashed potato, crushed peanuts, green chilli and cumin seeds.
Shape into small discs and brush with oil.
Air fry at 190°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden and crisp.
Serve with curd or chutney.
Note: sabudana needs overnight soaking, not counted in active prep time above.
why_it_works: Vada (patty) format eaten with chutney is genuinely different from the soft, spoonable khichdi version already in the database
Air frying keeps this far lower in fat than the traditional deep-fried version
Same fasting-day ingredient, different construction and cooking method

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Semolina Cutlet
description: A pan-fried cutlet made from cooked rava (semolina) mixed with vegetables — a solid cutlet format distinct from rava idli or rava upma.
instructions: Cook rava with water and finely chopped vegetables into a thick, dry mixture; cool completely (this is essential for shaping).
Shape into small flat cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides.
Serve with ketchup or chutney.
why_it_works: Solid cutlet format is a genuinely different use of rava from the soft idli or loose upma preparations already in the database
Good make-ahead option since the rava mixture needs to cool before shaping anyway
Kid-friendly, familiar comfort food

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Idiyappam Bowl
description: Steamed rice-flour string hoppers (idiyappam) tossed with a light vegetable stir-fry — a distinct noodle-like format not used anywhere else in the database.
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water into a smooth, pliable dough.
Press through an idiyappam press (or a fine sieve) directly into a steamer plate to form noodle strands, and steam for 8-10 minutes.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, saute vegetables 3-4 minutes.
Gently toss the steamed idiyappam strands with the vegetables.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: String-hopper texture is entirely unlike any dosa, idli or roti already in the database
Steamed, essentially fat-free base
Kerala/Tamil Nadu home-style breakfast rarely represented in fitness recipe collections

name: ZITLAS Egg Idiyappam Bowl
description: Steamed idiyappam string hoppers tossed with scrambled egg — a protein-added variant of the Vegetable Idiyappam Bowl, using the same steaming technique.
instructions: Knead rice flour with boiling water into a smooth dough and press into idiyappam strands; steam for 8-10 minutes.
Heat oil, saute onion, then scramble in the beaten egg until just cooked.
Gently toss the steamed idiyappam strands with the scrambled egg.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Egg addition raises the protein of the same idiyappam base meaningfully above the vegetable-only version
Distinct from every other egg preparation in the database by the noodle-like idiyappam texture
Same steaming technique, different finishing

name: ZITLAS Air-Fried Chana Dal Vada
description: Chana dal ground and shaped into vadas, air-fried and served dry — a distinct dal and format from the urad dal vada bowl earlier in this batch.
ingredients: Chana dal, soaked and coarsely ground — 100 g
instructions: Coarsely grind soaked chana dal (keep it chunky, not smooth) with green chilli.
Mix in onion and fennel seeds.
Shape into small discs and brush with oil.
Air fry at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping once, until golden.
Serve with coconut or mint chutney.
why_it_works: Chana dal gives a chunkier, nuttier vada than the smooth urad dal version, a genuinely different texture
Fennel seed seasoning is a distinct flavour choice from the ginger-based urad version
Air fried, far lower fat than deep frying

name: ZITLAS Roasted Soybean Trail Mix Bowl
description: Whole roasted soybeans mixed with raisins — a dry, portable bowl using whole soybeans, distinct from the soya chunks, granules or flour used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Combine roasted whole soybeans and raisins in a small container.
Mix well.
Carry and eat on the move, or as a sit-down bowl.
why_it_works: Whole roasted soybeans have a different fat and fiber profile from the defatted soya chunks or granules used in every other soya recipe here
Entirely dry and shelf-stable, no refrigeration needed
Genuinely no prep beyond mixing

name: ZITLAS Rajma Poha Cutlet Sandwich
description: Leftover rajma bound with crushed poha instead of oats, shaped into cutlets and sandwiched — a distinct binder choice from the Rajma Oats Tikki Sandwich already in the database.
instructions: Mash leftover rajma with crushed poha and chilli powder — the poha absorbs moisture and binds the mixture.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp on both sides.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Poha as a binder gives a noticeably different texture (softer, slightly sticky) from the oats-bound version already in the database
Third genuinely different way to use leftover rajma across the database (paratha, oats tikki, and now poha cutlet)
Good use of two leftovers at once if the poha is also left over

name: ZITLAS Boiled Peanut Chaat Bowl
description: Peanuts boiled (not roasted) and tossed chaat-style — a South Indian coastal technique giving a softer, different texture from every roasted-peanut use in the database.
ingredients: Raw peanuts, boiled in shell and shelled — 80 g
instructions: Pressure cook raw peanuts in their shells with water and a little salt for 3-4 whistles until soft; cool and shell them.
Toss the boiled peanuts with onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Serve at room temperature.
why_it_works: Boiling peanuts gives a completely different, softer texture from every roasted-peanut preparation elsewhere in the database
A genuinely different technique, not just a renamed roasted-peanut chaat
Coastal South Indian street-food style

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Kanji Drink
description: A traditional fermented, mildly spiced vegetable drink (kanji) made with mustard and beetroot — a fermented probiotic drink format used nowhere else in the database.
ingredients: Black salt, red chilli powder — 4 g
instructions: Combine sliced beetroot, water, ground mustard, black salt and chilli powder in a glass jar.
Cover and leave to ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, stirring once daily.
Once mildly sour and tangy, strain and refrigerate.
Serve chilled, a small glass at a time.
Note: fermentation takes 2-3 days; active prep time above covers assembly only.
why_it_works: A genuinely fermented, probiotic drink — a category not represented anywhere else in the database
